title: Tajadura-Jiménez 2009 · earlobe detection and sound spectrum
citation: Tajadura-Jiménez, A., Kitagawa, N., Väljamäe, A., Zampini, M., Murray, M. M., & Spence, C. (2009). Auditory–somatosensory multisensory interactions are spatially modulated by stimulated body surface and acoustic spectra. Neuropsychologia, 47(1), 195–205.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.response: Respond rapidly to any sound, touch or paired event with a button held in the right hand. The analysis retains reaction times between 150 and 1000 ms.
published_method.analysis: Compare paired RTs with each modality alone, including response distributions and a probability-summation prediction. This static-distance design does not fit a continuous boundary.
published_method.geometry: Touch the lower tip of one earlobe. Set static speakers 20 cm to either side of the head center and 10 cm above the ear.

sound.version_caveat: Use the final journal’s high-band limit. The earlier ICAD report gives a 14000 Hz lower cutoff.

stimulus_type.value: Static loudspeaker noise bursts and electrocutaneous pulses
stimulus_type.source: Neuropsychologia pp. 197–198, §§2.3.1–2.3.4; Neuropsychologia pp. 196–197, Fig. 1 and §2.1.2; Neuropsychologia p. 197, §§2.1.3–2.1.4

value.level_reference: Measured at the participant's ear position
value.delivery: One custom loudspeaker per auditory-containing trial
value.lateral_coordinate_note: Signed lateral position uses negative for left as an encoding of the article’s named sides; these are head-center lateral offsets.
value.loudness_policy: Levels selected using ISO 226 equal-loudness curves. No participant-by-participant matching is reported.
